subject: Applied Calculus
sourceBasis: ACADRIX MA25C01 Unit IV notes and R-2025 syllabus: iterated/double integrals, change of order, Cartesian/polar coordinates, triple integrals, cylindrical and spherical coordinate systems.
note: Original ACADRIX exam-practice problems. These are not claimed official university questions unless separately verified.

questions.question: Evaluate a double integral over a rectangular region by writing the iterated integral, integrating with respect to the inner variable first, and simplifying the final result.
solutionPlan: Choose and write the order of integration.
Evaluate the inner integral treating the other variable as constant.
Apply the outer limits and simplify.

questions.question: Given a double integral whose limits describe a non-rectangular region, sketch the region, change the order of integration, derive the new limits and evaluate the integral.
solutionPlan: Sketch the region and mark every boundary.
Derive its lower and upper boundaries.

questions.question: Evaluate a double integral over a circular disk using polar coordinates, including transformation of the integrand, limits and Jacobian.
solutionPlan: Use x=r cosθ and y=r sinθ.
Convert x²+y² to r² where applicable.
Set r and θ limits from the geometry.
Replace dA by r dr dθ.

questions.question: Evaluate a double integral over a sector or other circularly bounded planar region using suitable polar limits.
solutionPlan: Find the radial boundary for each angle.
Evaluate and check the geometric meaning.

questions.question: Formulate and evaluate the area of a plane region using a double integral, choosing Cartesian or polar coordinates according to the boundary geometry.
solutionPlan: Choose coordinates that simplify the boundaries.
Evaluate and interpret the result as area.

questions.question: Evaluate a triple integral over a solid bounded by Cartesian planes or surfaces using Cartesian coordinates.
solutionPlan: Evaluate from the innermost integral outward.

questions.question: Evaluate a triple integral over a solid with cylindrical symmetry using cylindrical coordinates.
solutionPlan: Use x=r cosθ and y=r sinθ.
Determine r, θ and z limits.
Evaluate and check the volume or accumulated quantity.

questions.question: Evaluate a triple integral over a spherical region using spherical coordinates, including correct angular limits and Jacobian.
solutionPlan: Use x=ρ sinφ cosθ, y=ρ sinφ sinθ and z=ρ cosφ.
Determine ρ, φ and θ limits.
Use dV=ρ² sinφ dρ dφ dθ.

questions.question: Use a triple integral in spherical coordinates to formulate and evaluate the volume of a sphere of radius a.
solutionPlan: Integrate ρ² sinφ over the full spherical limits.
Simplify the result and identify the geometric volume.

questions.question: Use cylindrical coordinates to formulate and evaluate the volume of a circular cylinder about the z-axis.
solutionPlan: Set radial, angular and vertical limits from the cylinder.
Compare the result with the expected geometric volume.

questions.question: Formulate a triple-integral expression for the total mass of a solid when its volume density is given, and evaluate it using the coordinate system that matches the geometry.
solutionPlan: Describe the solid and choose coordinates.

questions.question: For a given three-dimensional solid, justify the choice between Cartesian, cylindrical and spherical coordinates and formulate the corresponding triple integral.
solutionPlan: Choose the coordinate system that simplifies the limits.
Set limits and formulate the integral.

questions.question: Convert a double integral containing x²+y² and circular boundaries into polar coordinates and evaluate it completely.
solutionPlan: Convert the circular boundary to r-limits.

questions.question: For an integral whose original order produces difficult inner limits, reconstruct the region, reverse the order and evaluate the resulting simpler iterated integral.
solutionPlan: Sketch the region rather than merely swapping symbols.
Write the reversed integral or sum of integrals.

questions.question: For a region that can be described in more than one coordinate system, formulate the multiple integral in two coordinate systems and explain which is more efficient for evaluation.
solutionPlan: Select and evaluate the simpler form where required.

examChecklist: Sketch the region or solid before deriving limits.
Never reverse integration order by merely swapping dx and dy.
For polar coordinates use dA=r dr dθ.
For cylindrical coordinates use dV=r dr dθ dz.
For spherical coordinates use dV=ρ²sinφ dρ dφ dθ.
Check limits against the geometry before evaluating.
For integrand 1, verify area or volume when possible.
